uncited: Unlike its siblings, it explicitly preserves directional visibility information during mipmap generation to mitigate artifacts inherent in standard isotropic pre-integration [2552-voxel-cone-tracing-anisotropic-filtering.md].

This representation prevents color mixing and opacity under-estimation during MIP-mapping by integrating values along specific axes, allowing for accurate interpolation of lighting at render time [4963-anisotropic-voxel-representation.md].
For each non-leaf voxel, the six directional values are computed by performing a step of volumetric integration in depth for each direction [4963-anisotropic-voxel-representation.md].
This involves compositing the 8 child voxels front-to-back along the specific axis [2552-voxel-cone-tracing-anisotropic-filtering.md].
The results are averaged to produce the final directional value for the parent voxel [4963-anisotropic-voxel-representation.md].

During cone tracing, the voxel value is retrieved by linearly interpolating the values from the three closest directions with respect to the view direction $\vec{v}$ [4963-anisotropic-voxel-representation.md].
Directional values are only computed and used for voxels not located in the last octree level (not at full resolution) [4963-anisotropic-voxel-representation.md].
Leaf nodes store only the standard single value [4963-anisotropic-voxel-representation.md].
Storing directional values for all properties increases memory consumption by 1.5x compared to isotropic [2552-voxel-cone-tracing-anisotropic-filtering.md].
The base level of the mipmap is identical for all directions and can be shared, reducing the cost from 6x to 1.5x [2552-voxel-cone-tracing-anisotropic-filtering.md].
